problem: The classical cost is left vague ('may need many inputs'). For Deutsch-Jozsa the standard worst-case deterministic count is exact and small enough to state: 2^(n−1)+1 queries (and 2 queries for the one-bit Deutsch case). Leaving it out weakens the speed-up claim students are asked to remember.
fix: Classically, a deterministic check needs 2 queries in the one-bit case and up to 2^(n−1)+1 queries in the n-bit case in the worst case; the quantum circuit needs one.

problem: The note on the oracle node says 'oracle with ancilla |1⟩'. At the moment the oracle acts, the ancilla has already passed through H and is |−⟩=(|0⟩−|1⟩)/√2, not |1⟩. A student reading the figure left to right will picture U_f acting on |1⟩ and miss the phase-kickback preparation, which the exam traps themselves stress.
fix: Change the note to 'oracle with ancilla already in |−⟩' (the ancilla is prepared in |1⟩ and Hadamarded before U_f).
